sources.articleTitle: 'Hopeful they will come': India on inviting Pak to SCO Civilisational Forum in Delhi
China, Kazakhstan, Iran, others confirm participation in SCO Civilisational Forum, says Gajendra Shekhawat

headline: India Invites Pakistan To Attend Inaugural SCO Civilisational Forum
seoTitle: India Invites Pakistan To SCO Civilisational Forum
metaDescription: India has formally invited Pakistan to join the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, with officials expressing hope for attendance.
aiSummaryBullets: India will host the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi from November 20 to 22.
Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat stated that several nations, including China, Kazakhstan, and Iran, have confirmed participation.
The Indian government has extended an invitation to Pakistan and remains hopeful that representatives will attend the cultural event.
aiContextParagraph: The inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum is scheduled to take place in New Delhi from November 20 to 22, 2026. According to Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, the event is designed to facilitate discussions regarding shared civilisational heritage and cultural ties among member nations. Several countries, such as China, Kazakhstan, and Iran, have officially confirmed their attendance at the event held at Bharat Mandapam. During a recent media briefing, Minister Shekhawat noted that India has extended an invitation to Pakistan to participate in the dialogue. While acknowledging that a confirmation from Pakistan is still pending, the minister expressed optimism regarding their potential attendance at the forum. This event represents a significant diplomatic engagement under the auspices of the SCO framework, focusing on historical and cultural exchanges rather than traditional political or security-related matters among the diverse group of participating Eurasian states.
whyItIsViral: The story gained moderate visibility due to the diplomatic implications of India inviting Pakistan to a high-profile international event in New Delhi.
